signals.name: Nathan Benaich
signals.summary: Secondary summaries say the 2026 State of AI Report, which Benaich edits, came out Oct 8. It covers the frontier-lab race, Chinese open-weight models, agents with recursive self-improvement, physical AI, sovereign AI and US export controls. I did not check the report itself, and I found none of Benaich's own posts.
signals.connection: The export-control and China open-weight sections tie to the China and AI-governance topics. The AI-financing worries behind the memory chip selloff relate to the report's frontier-scaling theme.

signals.name: Ben Thompson
signals.latest_title: SpaceX Buys More Spectrum, Musk and Market Structure, Distributed Cellular
signals.summary: Thompson says SpaceX's mobile strategy is becoming clearer with its latest spectrum purchase, and that it might work. His weekly roundup (2026.41, Oct 9) covered drifting apart from Apple, Facebook complications and the absurdity of US-China dynamics.
signals.connection: Links to Applied Tech & Industry and Frontier Tech. His roundup's US-China theme touches the China topic.

signals.name: Packy McCormick
signals.latest_title: Runway: Learning From Watching the World
signals.summary: Packy co-wrote an essay with Runway co-CEO Anastasis Germanidis on Runway's approach to learning from watching the world. His Weekly Dose of Optimism #214 (Oct 9) covered the Nobel, Matter Compiler, an Anduril shipyard, a mouth cancer patch and the Biohub Virtual Cell.
signals.connection: Links to Frontier Tech / AI. The Anduril shipyard item touches Defense & Security and Applied Tech & Industry.

signals.name: Lenny Rachitsky
signals.latest_title: How to tell if a startup has a moat
signals.summary: Lenny gives a framework for judging whether a company you're considering joining is built to last. He also published a How I AI episode with Meta Design Director Alex Cornell on how Meta designed Muse, an AI agent meant to work through one interface for both non-technical people and engineers.
signals.connection: The moat framework fits the AI-financing worries and the question of which AI companies last. Meta's Muse relates to Frontier Tech / AI and Labor & Workforce.
